articleTitle: Reliability in testing techniques for precision Zener diodes
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Reliable Electronic Measurements
abstract: A voltage measurement system is described which can measure at the 5 V to 8 V level with a resolution of 1 mu V and a long term uncertainty of 3 p.p.m. A microcomputer controls the three stage measurement process incorporating the techniques of a metrology lab. Reliability of measurement is ensured by repeated measurements and by duplicated paths to trace the voltage being measured back to the standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic self-test provides improved accuracy and user confidence
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Reliable Electronic Measurements
abstract: Developments in the field of automated modulation measurement have produced units with significantly improved accuracies (+or-0.5%) which can confidently be used for a wide range of measurements. The improvement in operating speed combined with the possibility of controlling the measurements via the general purpose interface bus (GPIB) allows a significant increase in efficiency and frees the measurement engineer from an otherwise tedious task. The improved measuring accuracy has been achieved by improvements in circuit techniques and by the provision of built-in calibration capabilities. These techniques bring real user benefits in terms of improved consistency and accuracy, greater user confidence and the possibility of automatic fault identification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Can reliability mean a life-time operation without a failure?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Reliable Electronic Measurements
abstract: The increased use of complex and application specific integrated circuits has led to a dramatic reduction in component count, with a substantial improvement in reliability. It is suggested that knowledge exists to improve the design and manufacturing process to make zero defects a realistic target. Software correction techniques for measurement and calibration have played an important role in improving both reliability and performance. Future innovations will be directed towards producing smart instruments which automatically prevent misuse and eliminate avoidable errors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quality assurance requirements for the management of measuring and test equipment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Reliable Electronic Measurements
abstract: It is suggested that all measurement standards and measuring equipment should be calibrated using measurement standards that are traceable to international measurement standards, or to national measurement standards that are consistent with the recommendations of the CGPM (General Conference on Weights and Measures). In cases where such national or international measurement standards do not exist (for example, for hardness), traceability should be established to other measurement standards (for example, industry standards) that are internationally accepted in the field concerned.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave sweep generator uses digital control and automatic calibration to enhance measurement reliability
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Reliable Electronic Measurements
abstract: The author introduces some novel digital techniques used to control the operation of a microwave sweep generator. It is shown how, together with an automatic calibration facility, these techniques contribute to an increase in measurement reliability and provide a flexibility of operation not previously available with more traditional designs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement integrity, equipment availability and economic support
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Reliable Electronic Measurements
abstract: The author is concerned with an appraisal of the complexity of test equipment, relating the measurement integrity needs of an organization, to the economic choices available, consistent with the need to seek a minimum real cost support solution. A review is made of the factors affecting the increasing complexity of test equipment, focusing on the decreasing cost of firmware as the principle driving force in the introduction of increasingly more sophisticated and complex equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving the accuracy of measurement in component meters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Reliable Electronic Measurements
abstract: Discusses the development of instruments for establishing the values of practical inductors, capacitors and resistors. The equivalent circuit of a component arrived at from physical considerations can be reduced to one resistive and one reactive component that together produce the same magnitude and phase relationships between current and voltage in a circuit as would the component itself. The equivalent resistive and reactive elements which are measured at the terminals of a complex impedance/admittance measuring system, such as a modern electronic component meter, are discussed. Measurement strategies are proposed that lead to improved accuracy of measurement, particularly of the minor component that often limits the accuracy of measurement of 'loss angle' for example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
